description: Route-level bundle size budgets for authenticated Next.js pages. Budgets cover the First Load JS (shared chunks + page chunk) for each route segment. Values are in bytes. Measured values are filled by the post-build bundle analyzer and compared against the declared ceiling by the orchestrator. A null measured value means the route has not been profiled yet.

network.mobile: ~1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 150ms RTT — close to Fast 3G+ (browser-driver.mjs hardcoded: 1,600,000/8 bytes/s down, 750,000/8 bytes/s up, 150ms latency)

cpu.mobile: 4x CPU slowdown (Chrome DevTools mid-tier mobile preset)

referenceProfile.notes: Measured with Lighthouse 12 in CI using the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Field data (CrUX) is the source of truth for production; lab data here is the gating proxy. The 100ms responsiveness rule (CLAUDE.md §12.2) is enforced by INP ≤ 200ms. Bundle bytes are gzip-compressed sizes (level 9) summed over all unique chunks referenced in each route's page_client-reference-manifest.js from a production pnpm build. measuredPageChunkBytes is the route-specific additive (chunks not shared with /dashboard baseline).

/mail.note: Mail shell — first-load budget is higher because DOMPurify (isomorphic-dompurify) is a non-trivial dependency; compose sheet, AI toolbar and inbox summary sheet are lazy-loaded via next/dynamic. PASSES: 507kB < 614kB ceiling

/inbox.note: Home inbox — lightweight notification-style inbox; no external mail provider calls. PASSES: 461kB < 512kB ceiling. NotificationDetailDrawer is lazy (next/dynamic ssr:false); chunk is preloaded after mount to avoid INP spike on first interaction. Dashboard baseline is 489kB (40 shared chunks).

/build/inbox._routeNote: Route is /build/inbox not /build/[projectId]/inbox — corrected from original declaration
/build/inbox.note: Build module approval inbox. PASSES: 463kB < 614kB ceiling. InboxTicketPreview (ticket detail components) is lazy (next/dynamic ssr:false).

/crm/inbox.note: CRM inbox — deals and contact conversations. PASSES: 487kB < 614kB ceiling

/dashboard.note: Home dashboard — the shared-chunk baseline every other route's measuredPageChunkBytes is taken against, so its page-only additive is 0 by definition.
